task.description:
Validate the CODE-DESIGNER Step 01 design for PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 (events table monthly range partitioning -- high risk, core table). Standard checks apply (every AC traced, no implementation code, tools/lint_design_artefact.py clean). CRITICAL ADDITIONAL CHECK: both PAR-01 and PAR-03 design docs flag that src/event_store/store.zig::Store.archive() currently issues DELETE FROM events / DELETE FROM events_archive-adjacent statements that become actively incompatible with PAR-03's own AC ("No DELETE statement SHALL run against events or events_archive at any point") the moment PAR-03 ships. Both docs recommend deferring archive()'s retirement/rewrite as a follow-up rather than fixing it in this batch, reasoning that PAR-01's ACs don't mention archive() and PAR-03's ACs govern the NEW retention mechanism, not the old one. Assess this reasoning carefully: does PAR-03's AC ("No DELETE... at any point") actually mean literally zero DELETE statements can exist in the codebase touching these tables once PAR-03 ships (in which case archive() being left as-is would make this batch's own release FALSELY claim AC compliance, since archive() would still be callable and would still violate it), or does it mean PAR-03's OWN mechanism specifically never deletes (a narrower, correct-as-designed reading)? This determines whether deferring archive() is safe or is a hidden AC violation. If genuinely ambiguous, this may need to route to REQ-ANALYST rather than being decided unilaterally by either CODE-DESIGNER or you.

RE-VALIDATION (after REWORK 1): CODE-DESIGNER added the RetentionClassForbidden guard (app-level in Registry.registerType() + a DB-level CHECK constraint backstop) and specified FULL REMOVAL of Store.archive() (confirmed zero src/ call sites), since it drives 4 traced test cases for ES-07 (SHOULD, RELEASED) and ADP-11 (MUST, RELEASED) -- TC-ES-07-01, TC-ES-07-02, TC-ADP-11-02, TC-ADP-11-03. The design specifies these 4 tests be REWRITTEN to assert archive() is retired and repointed at PAR-03's own new PartitionRetention mechanism, in the SAME batch/commit. CRITICAL RE-VALIDATION FOCUS: does this design genuinely keep ES-07 and ADP-11 (both already-RELEASED requirements) satisfied after the rewrite, or does retiring archive() risk silently regressing a released requirement's actual guaranteed behavior? Read ES-07 and ADP-11's full requirement bodies and their existing (soon-to-be-rewritten) AC mappings in tests/specs/ES-07.md and tests/specs/ADP-11.md (if they exist) before judging this. This is the single most important thing to verify in this re-validation -- a design that retires code satisfying one requirement in order to satisfy a different requirement's AC, without genuinely proving the first requirement still holds, would be trading one compliance gap for another.
acceptance_criteria: Every AC in PAR-01, PAR-02, PAR-03, PAR-04 traced to a design section
No implementation code in the design
Migration approach correctly scoped as fresh-schema-only (not attempting PAR-05's online conversion)
Current events/events_archive shape preservation verified against actual migration history

Store.archive() vs PAR-03 DELETE-prohibition conflict explicitly resolved: either confirmed genuinely non-blocking with sound reasoning, or flagged as requiring REQ-ANALYST clarification before BACKEND-DEV proceeds

result.summary: RE-VALIDATION (after REWORK 1) FAIL. RetentionClassForbidden guard (PAR-03 AC1) is genuinely closed: app-level check in Registry.validateRegisterParams() + DB-level chk_retention_class_protected_family CHECK constraint, added atomically in the same migration/commit, matches docs/anti-patterns.md's CHECK/application-constant rule. TC-ES-07-01/02 rewrite (ES-07, SHOULD) and TC-ADP-11-03 rewrite (protected keep_days archive path) are sound: PAR-03's DETACH/ATTACH mechanism genuinely delivers the same guarantee ES-07/ADP-11 require for retain_forever/archive_queryable classes (rows moved, never deleted, remain queryable), just at partition-month granularity instead of row granularity -- an acceptable mechanism swap since neither AC mandates row-level implementation. BUT TC-ADP-11-02 rewrite is NOT equivalent and represents a genuine regression, not a mechanism swap. TC-ADP-11-02 proves ADP-11's 'non-protected ES-07 hard-delete configurability preserved' acceptance area: a non-protected event type configured hard_delete_days is genuinely removed with ZERO archive copy (events=0, events_archive=0) -- true row-level DELETE, which is semantically distinct from archive_queryable/retain_forever. The ONLY PAR-03 mechanism capable of true deletion is events_ephemeral's DROP TABLE path, which requires the event to have been ROUTED to events_ephemeral at append time based on retention_class='delete' -- docs/processes/system/event-log-partitioning.md Step 7 explicitly assigns 'Event Store routes each append by the event type's retention class' to requirement PAR-03. Grepped Store.append() (src/event_store/store.zig:236) and confirmed zero retention-class-based routing exists today, and NONE of the four design docs in this batch (par-01, par-02, par-03, par-04) specify or schedule this routing change as in-scope work. PAR-03's design mentions the routing gap only once, in passing ('nothing currently routes an event to events_ephemeral except by consulting this column'), never as a blocking gap for the archive() removal it specifies. Net effect: once Store.archive() is deleted per this design's own removal scope, the platform has NO mechanism left by which any event type -- protected or not -- can ever reach events_ephemeral or genuine hard-deletion, because nothing writes there. This silently eliminates real hard-delete capability for non-protected types entirely (not a granularity change, a capability disappearance) until a future, currently-unscoped change adds retention_class-based routing to Store.append(). TC-ADP-11-02, as specified to be repointed at PartitionRetention.runEphemeralDrop(), cannot actually pass in a real system after archive() is removed, because no path populates events_ephemeral for it to drop -- the rewritten test would either be vacuously true (asserting a drop of an always-empty/never-populated partition) or would require test-only routing code that doesn't reflect production Store.append() behavior. This is exactly the anti-pattern this validation exists to catch: retiring code that satisfies one released requirement (ADP-11's non-protected hard-delete configurability) in order to satisfy a different requirement's AC (PAR-03's DELETE-prohibition), without proving the first requirement still holds end-to-end. Standard checks otherwise clean: tools/lint_design_artefact.py passes 0 issues on all 4 Type E design docs (par-01/02/03/04) and both migration YAMLs; tools/codegen_migration.py --dry-run exits 0 for both templates/specs/par-02-partition-catalog.migration.yaml and templates/specs/par-03-retention-class.migration.yaml, output matches the design's documented CUSTOM-block approach.

issues.description: PAR-03's design specifies removing Store.archive() and repointing TC-ADP-11-02 (ADP-11, MUST, RELEASED -- 'non-protected ES-07 hard-delete configurability preserved') at PartitionRetention.runEphemeralDrop(), but no design artifact in this batch (par-01, par-02, par-03, or par-04) specifies the append-time routing logic that decides whether a given event is written to events or events_ephemeral based on event_type_registry.retention_class. docs/processes/system/event-log-partitioning.md Step 7 assigns exactly this routing to PAR-03 ('Event Store routes each append by the event type's retention class'), but PAR-03's design never implements or schedules it -- Store.append() (src/event_store/store.zig:236) has zero retention-class awareness today, confirmed by reading the function. Without this routing, events_ephemeral is never populated by any code path, so runEphemeralDrop()'s DROP TABLE has nothing to ever drop for a retention_class='delete' type, and the rewritten TC-ADP-11-02 cannot exercise real hard-delete behavior against production code. Net effect: removing archive() in this batch, as currently scoped, eliminates the platform's only working hard-delete mechanism for non-protected event types and replaces it with nothing -- a silent regression of ADP-11's released guarantee, not a mechanism swap.

Because the append-time routing gap above is unaddressed, the design's instruction to rewrite TC-ADP-11-02 in this same batch (see PAR-03 design's 'Store.archive() retirement' section, bullet 3) cannot be carried out as specified: TEST-DESIGNER has no real routing mechanism to write an integration test against for the non-protected hard-delete case. This must be resolved (either by adding Store.append() retention-class routing to this same batch's scope, or by revising the removal/test-rewrite plan) before BACKEND-DEV can implement Step 2a without producing a test that is either vacuous or exercises test-only code paths.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER (REWORK 2) to close the events_ephemeral append-time routing gap: either add Store.append() retention_class-based routing to this batch's PAR-03 (or a companion) design so TC-ADP-11-02's rewrite can exercise real production behavior, or revise the archive() removal scope/timing so ADP-11's non-protected hard-delete guarantee is not left unimplemented at any point this batch could ship.
